transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you into the clinic today?

Thank you. Well, what brings me in is... I guess I've just stopped wanting to do the things that usually keep me going. It's hard to explain, but I just don't have the drive for any of it anymore. 

Like going to salsa nights, or church gatherings, or even cooking for the neighbors. I'm a carpenter, and usually, I love just walking out into my shop to enjoy the smell of the wood. But lately, I don't even want to do that. I just don't have any interest in any of it right now.
How long have you been feeling this loss of interest?

It's been about two months now. This whole change in my mood and how I'm acting... it all started right around the time my wife's health suddenly declined. Our whole daily routine changed because of it, and I've just been stuck feeling this way ever since.
Along with this loss of interest, have you also been feeling down, sad, or hopeless most days?

Yeah, I have. Honestly... most mornings I wake up with this heavy, empty feeling right in my chest. It's like the color has just gone out of the house. I feel incredibly down, and I really have to force myself not to break down in front of my wife. So, yes, that sadness is definitely there most days.
Have you ever experienced a period of feeling this down or losing interest like this at any other point in your life?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had bad days here and there, like anyone else, but nothing like this. This is... this is the first time it's been this heavy and lasted this long. I've never felt this kind of emptiness before.
Have you ever had a period of time when you felt the opposite—unusually energetic, high, or on top of the world?

Actually, yeah. Right at the beginning of all this, I did have these stretches where I felt really fired up. Like I was almost unstoppable. But... I was also pretty on edge. If my wife or one of the guys on my crew questioned me about anything, I would just snap at them over absolutely nothing. So, yeah, I guess I did feel like that for a bit.
How long did that period of feeling fired up and unstoppable last?

I'm honestly not sure. I wasn't exactly keeping track of the days when it was happening. It was just... a stretch of time where I felt like that, and then it passed. So I really couldn't give you an exact number of days or anything.
During that stretch when you felt so fired up, did you find you could get by on much less sleep than usual without feeling tired?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I've always been an early riser for work, being on the job sites and all, but I was still getting my regular hours in. I didn't notice needing less sleep or running on empty without being tired. I'm pretty sure my sleep was just normal during that time.
During that stretch when you felt so fired up, did you experience your thoughts racing or jumping very quickly from one idea to another?

No, not really. I mean, I had a lot of drive to get things done on the job, but my mind wasn't spinning or jumping around like that. I was just thinking normally... just maybe a bit more focused on the work in front of me. So no, I wouldn't say my thoughts were racing.
Over these past two months, have you been having any trouble with your sleep?

No, not really. I mean... I sleep about the same as I always do. I get tired after a long day, go to bed, and wake up early for work like normal. So, no, I haven't noticed any real trouble with it lately.
Over these past two months, have you noticed any significant drop in your energy levels or felt unusually fatigued?

Yeah, I have. Honestly, even after sitting down to rest or getting a full night in bed, my body just feels completely worn out. It's like I've been framing a roof all day long, even when I haven't. Just doing small chores... like loading my tools into the truck in the morning... it just feels like too much to handle lately.
Have you noticed any difficulty concentrating, focusing on tasks, or making everyday decisions lately?

Yeah, it's been pretty bad actually. I'll be on a job site, and... well, I stare at blueprints I've read my whole life, and the lines just blur together in my head. It's like I can't make sense of them anymore. I end up having to ask the younger guys to repeat things or check my work, stuff I should understand right away. It's frustrating, but I just can't seem to hold my focus on it.
Have you been feeling down on yourself, experiencing feelings of worthlessness, or blaming yourself for things lately?

Yeah... I have been. I just... I keep replaying every doctor's appointment, every little change in my wife's health before she passed. I can't stop telling myself that a better husband would have caught it sooner, you know? That I should have protected her somehow. It's just a heavy feeling of guilt that I can't shake.
Have you had any thoughts of wanting to end your life, or wishing you wouldn't wake up?

Yeah... I have. I've had thoughts that... well, maybe it would just be easier if I went to sleep and didn't wake up. And sometimes I catch myself thinking that my family might actually be better off without me around. Honestly, it scares me when my mind goes there, but... yeah, those thoughts are there.
